why: 1.71 K of self-heating does not 'eat most of' a class tolerance; it exceeds the whole IEC 60751 class B tolerance at 95 C (and twice class A). The output q_selfheat.txt has the same wording ('eats most of a class tolerance') in companion/ch34/examples_q.py.

why: examples_n.soe(): event A's time ta is floored to its bin BEFORE the gap is added (tb_true = ta + gap + clock), so every first event sits at the start of a bin. That inflates 'same stamp' at 10 ms to 96 % (correct about 50 %) and at 1 ms to 8 % (correct about 5 %), and 'wrong order' to 2.0 % (correct 0.6 % at 1 ms, 0.06 % at 10 ms; the 2 % is the share whose true arrival order is reversed by the 0.5 ms sync error, most of which then share a stamp). Fix: t = rng.uniform(0,1000,n); ta = floor(t/res)*res; tb = floor((t+gap+clock)/res)*res. Re-run n_soe.txt and update exm-ch34-soe and exr-ch34-127.
evidence: Recomputed with seed 345: res 1 ms same 5.05 %, recorded reversed 0.62 %; res 10 ms same 49.8 %, reversed 0.06 %; true reversal by clock error 1.96 % in both.

old: و $t_\text{ta}$ زمانِ برگشت در هر دستگاه است.
new: و $t_\text{ta}$ زمانِ برگشت در هر دستگاه است. ضریبِ ۸ برای پیوندِ همگامی مانندِ اترنت درست است. روی خطِ سریالِ ناهمگام، مانندِ [RS-485]{.ltr}، هر بایت با بیتِ آغاز، بیتِ توازن یا بیتِ پایان ۱۰ تا ۱۱ بیت می‌شود و فاصلهٔ سکوتِ میانِ قاب‌ها هم افزوده می‌شود. با ۱۱ بیت، چرخهٔ ۳۰ کنتورِ @exm-ch35-serial حدودِ [2.3 s]{.ltr} است، نه [1.77 s]{.ltr}.
why: The poll-cycle formula multiplies bytes by 8 bits, but on asynchronous serial lines (RS-485, Modbus RTU) each byte is sent as a 10- or 11-bit character (start bit, 8 data bits, parity and/or stop), plus an inter-frame silence; the cycle times quoted (1.77 s, 1.11 s at 19200, P01 53.3 ms) are therefore about 25-40 % too short. Least invasive fix is a stated caveat; alternatively change the factor in plantp.scada and the outputs.
evidence: 53 bytes x 11 bits / 9600 = 60.7 ms + 15 ms = 75.7 ms; x 30 = 2.27 s (10 bits: 2.11 s). Modbus over Serial Line V1.02: RTU character = 11 bits; 3.5-character silent interval between frames.

why: 3.5e9 x 8 / 1e8 = 280 s, not 276 s; 276 s comes from the unrounded 3.456 GB (2,000 tags x 86,400 s x 20 B).
